scanPrep.context:
Summary: Audited BrokenCrystals (NestJS/Fastify) app and confirmed no rate limiting, account lockout, reachable CAPTCHA, IP allowlisting, or WAF/request-filtering exists that would block a DAST scanner; no changes were necessary.
Recovery guidance (security controls): Findings for future reference: (1) No ThrottlerModule/express-rate-limit/rate-limit package in package.json or src, no 429/ThrottlerException code paths — verified live by firing 9 rapid identical POST /api/auth/login requests (admin/admin), all returned 201 with no throttling or error-body indicators. (2) No failed-login counter/lockout logic in AuthService/UsersController. (3) Keycloak realm-export.json has bruteForceProtected:false already, and the only CAPTCHA reference in the entire repo is Keycloak's 'registration-recaptcha-action' authenticator on the registration flow, whose requirement is already 'DISABLED' — so no reachable server-side CAPTCHA enforcement exists anywhere (app-level login has no CAPTCHA check at all). (4) CsrfGuard on POST /api/auth/login only triggers when body.op is 'csrf' or 'csrf_dom' (deliberate vulnerable-demo modes); the default/standard login mode is 'basic' and bypasses CSRF entirely, so standard automated login is unaffected; if a scan profile explicitly exercises the csrf/csrf_dom modes, the token is obtainable via GET /api/auth/simple-csrf-flow or /api/auth/dom-csrf-flow and can be replayed by a multistep auth object via NexTemplate + cookie replay, so no relaxation was needed or performed. (5) Keycloak session/token lifetimes (accessTokenLifespan 300s, ssoSessionIdleTimeout 1800s) are standard, non-aggressive defaults — left unchanged. (6) No IP allowlist/blocklist or WAF middleware found; 'trustProxy:true' is just for X-Forwarded-For parsing. If a future scan still encounters 429s or CAPTCHA challenges, re-check for a reverse proxy/CDN layer in front of localhost:3000 not represented in this compose file, and re-run the live rapid-POST test against the actual endpoint in use.
Recovery guidance (2FA/MFA): Investigation performed: searched the full TypeScript source tree and found no twoFactor/2fa/mfa/totp/otp/authenticator logic in the app's own auth code (src/auth/*, src/users/*, src/model/user.entity.ts). The only TOTP-related artifacts are in keycloak/imports/realm-export.json, where otpPolicyType=totp is merely an available realm credential type; the CONFIGURE_TOTP required action has defaultAction:false and no user in the realm export (or in the app's own 'user' Postgres table, seeded via pg.sql) has any requiredActions, totp flag, or status/locked/pending column set. The Postgres 'user' table schema itself has no 2FA-related columns at all (only email, password, is_admin, is_basic, etc.), confirming the app's native login path (POST /api/auth/login with body {user, password, op:'basic'}) never involves 2FA. Verified end-to-end: logging in as admin/admin returns HTTP 201 immediately with an Authorization JWT header (no 2FA prompt), and calling GET /api/users/me with that token returns HTTP 200 with real profile JSON ({firstName, lastName, id, isAdmin}), confirming the account is fully active and unblocked. If a future scan still reports 2FA-like blocking, check whether the OIDC/Keycloak login path (op: 'oidc') is being used instead of basic login — in that case, direct the scanner to use the basic login flow, or inspect the specific Keycloak user account's requiredActions via the Keycloak admin console/API (http://localhost:<keycloak-port>/admin) and clear any CONFIGURE_TOTP required action for that user.
